lines.note: Funhoina continues the preceding page's Funhoi family: a person lacking means or capacity. The close-up shows two tall s forms in Peſſoa, not a t; this differs from the compact ß in neceßa-.

runs.text: rio, ou de poder, & habilidade, ou arte pera

lines.note: Completes the range of lacks: power, skill, or craft. Restored habilidade from OCR babilidade; the initial h agrees with the repeated discussion on the preceding page.
Completes 'to do something'. The statement concerns capability as well as material poverty, so a narrowly financial reading of Funhoina would be incomplete.
Funhoini is the adverbial form of the preceding expression. It is separately printed without a new Portuguese gloss; no definition is invented.
Funhoiſa gives the nominal degree/state form. Its final ſa is meaningful Japanese morphology, not an alternative Portuguese word.
Funi (不二) is explained literally as Futatçu narazu, not being two. The dictionary immediately paraphrases this as unity rather than leaving the negation unexplained.
Completes the paraphrase 'be one single thing'. Both the numeral and restrictive ſò matter to the Japanese non-duality expression.
Funicu is rotten flesh, explained Cuſaritaru xiximura. The shishi element is flesh here, not necessarily a particular animal.
Completes podre, rotten. Italic S. is a usage label; it is not part of the Japanese noun or an additional sentence.

runs.text: Dignidade que dà o Rey, ou outro ſe-

lines.note: Funin denotes a dignity or appointment conferred by a king. This is the dictionary's specific sense, not simply the modern act of arriving at one's post.
Extends the granting authority to another great lord and specifies reward for service. The following Funin starts an example continued below.
Funin uo daſaruru is granting the dignity or rank. The -raruru expression is honorific in this context, not necessarily a passive grant being received.
Funjin, explained Miuo vaquru, concerns manifestation of a divided body (分身). Its religious interpretation is supplied by the following Fotoque clause.

runs.text: cia do Fotoque que ẽ varias partes ſẽdo o meſ

lines.note: The same Fotoque manifests in multiple places. The embedded Japanese name is visibly italic here and remains so; ẽ and ſẽdo are Portuguese nasal abbreviations.

runs.text: mo ſe manifeſta de diuerſas maneiras.

lines.note: Completes the definition: although the same being, it appears in diverse ways. This is the dictionary's explanatory account, not a separate theological claim added by the review.
Funmiǒ denotes clarity. Its nasal-plus-m spelling and caron are retained; do not normalize it to the familiar modern spelling of 分明.
Funmiǒna is the adjective, clear and manifest. Restored clara from OCR clura; the following manifesta confirms the intended Portuguese adjective.
Funmiǒni is the adverb, clearly. Adu. is italic grammatical metadata, not a Japanese reading unit.
Funnobi is stretching out the feet or legs, with inflections uru, ita as printed. The Portuguese comparison continues into a stretch or yawn-like bodily action.
The printed eſpriguiça describes stretching oneself. It is not modernized to espreguiça merely because the latter is more familiar.
Funnu is anger or indignation (憤怒), paraphrased Icari, icaru. S. is retained in italic as a usage label.
Funô and munô describe lacking arts or abilities. Both circumflexes are visible; their nasal consonants differ and should remain distinct.
Completes habilidades from the preceding row. This short fragment is Portuguese, not an independent Japanese entry.
Funôna is the adjectival counterpart. Idem refers to the preceding lack-of-ability definition rather than supplying a new meaning.
Funôni is the adverbial counterpart. The dictionary gives only Adu.; the review should not fabricate a fuller printed gloss.

runs.text: Certa laya de limos do mar. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: Funori names a kind of marine weed. The following Itẽ introduces a second related meaning, not another plant species.

runs.text: Certo grude que ſe faz deſtes limos.

lines.note: The second sense is glue or sizing made from that seaweed. This is consistent with funori's material use but the text itself supplies the connection.

runs.text: Certos bolinhos que fazem do ro-

lines.note: Funoyaqi is a preparation of small cakes. The ingredient term ro-lão is physically divided and should be read with the next row.

runs.text: lão da farinha aſados em panela, ou tacho.

lines.note: Completes the coarse flour/bran ingredient and cooking in a pot or pan. Preserve the printed single-long-s aſados instead of imposing modern assados.
Funpǒ concerns fragrance. Both Cǒbaxij and cǒbaxij show carons in enlargement; corrected the second OCR circumflex, retaining the repeated adjective rather than removing it as redundant.

The example Reiqio xiqirini introduces an excellent fragrance spreading strongly. Reiqio is likely the Sino-Japanese fragrance expression; its faint or absent length mark is not supplied from expectation.

runs.text: O excelente cheiro recẽde muito. S.

lines.note: Completes funpǒ ſu, emitting fragrance abundantly. Portuguese recẽde means giving off an odor; the nasal abbreviation and S. label are retained.
Funpun here means entangling or mingling, explained Maguire, maguiruru. This is distinct from the fragrance homonym below.

runs.text: & miſturarſe algũa multidão de couſas entre ſi.

lines.note: Completes the definition as many things mixing among themselves. The multiplicity is essential to the sense, not a single object being misplaced.
Funpuntaru yuqi describes thick, mingled falling snow. The adjectival -taru formation agrees with the attributive snow phrase.
Completes the snowy mixture explanation. It is a continuation of mui-ta, not a fresh statement about another substance.
A separate Funpun concerns fragrance. The unusual Cǒbaxixi, cǒbaxixi sequence is actually visible; retain it as printed rather than automatically changing both to cǒbaxij.

runs.text: ue, ou eſpalharſe o cheiro. S.

lines.note: Completes the sweet-fragrance/spreading-smell definition. This separates the aromatic homonym from the earlier mingling sense.
Funqi is a vessel for excrement, explained Funo vtçuuamono. Portuguese ſeruiço here denotes a chamber utensil, not abstract service.
Funran means confusion or disorder, with Maguire and midaruru as Japanese paraphrases. The Portuguese defines disturbance rather than necessarily armed conflict.
Restored contrariedade from OCR contrartedade. The phrase concerns opposed qualities; the ordinary Portuguese noun and the visible letters agree.
Adds another sense of mixed, disturbed activity. Item and the paragraph marker signal the extension; the insects specified next make it concrete.
Completes the examples with mosquitoes and bees. This supports swarming or confused mingling, not a metaphor arbitrarily supplied by the reviewer.
Funſui is water associated with dung, explicitly Funno mizzu. It must not be read as the modern fountain homophone merely from kana.
Funto denotes human or animal excrement. The Portuguese supplies both sources; the spelling animaes is preserved.
Adds dung and earth as a further sense. Restored the clearly printed ¶ before Item; this is not an inferred entry boundary.
Funxit means loss amid confusion (紛失), paraphrased Midare vxinǒ. The definition continues across the column boundary, so its final cou- is not a completed clause.

runs.text: ſa enuolta, ou de mistura com outras.

lines.note: Completes the preceding column's Funxit: something lost while mixed among other things. This physical first row is a continuation, not a new entry.

runs.text: Adu. Modo deſe fazer, ou a-

lines.note: Fupputo describes a sudden manner of appearing or rising. Adu. is italic metadata; the printed deſe grouping is kept.

runs.text: leuantar algũa couſa derepente como nacida,

lines.note: Completes suddenly arising, with nacida introducing a swelling/eruption-like example. Do not automatically reinterpret it as a person's birth.
Burbulha is another sudden-emergence example. The Japanese Fupputo monouo yǔ begins a separate illustrative use about speaking.

runs.text: He homem que fala ſem conſidera

lines.note: Fitogia completes 'a person who says things abruptly'. The Portuguese specifies lack of consideration, so this is more than merely fast speech.
Completes the alternative 'impetuously'. This explains the adverb's pragmatic sense without changing the Japanese spelling.
Fuqe is a muddy or boggy place. Fuqeni famaru starts the example of getting trapped in it; f in famaru is the period spelling for h.
Completes famaru and the bogging-down gloss. The visibly separated A tolar is retained rather than automatically joined.
Fuqe, uru, eta covers becoming old and the advancing night. The two modern senses of fukeru are explicitly brought together in this entry.

The literary example starts with Miya and võmacurauo, honorific on-makura. Enlargement shows the nasal abbreviation over o, not a caron denoting length; the Japanese construction supports the correction.
Cata-muqeſaxe tamayeba is the honorific reclining action, followed by everyone growing quiet. The older causative/honorific sequence is grammatical and should not be simplified.

runs.text: rite, yo ſudeni fuqeni qeri. Taif.

lines.note: The night had already grown late: yo ſudeni fuqeni qeri. Roman Taif. identifies the Taiheiki citation; its final period is included in the label.
The citation gives book 18 and translates Miya as Rainha. Preserve that printed Portuguese choice without treating it as independent proof of the figure's identity.

runs.text: doſe todos: fezſe quaſi alta noite. ¶

lines.note: Completes the quieting of everyone and late-night gloss, then begins Toxiga fuqeta. The new example returns to human age.
Toxiga fuqeta is being advanced in years. This confirms the first meaning of Fuqe rather than a different pronunciation.
Fǔqei is scenery or the appearance of a place, paraphrased Tocorono qexiqi. The u caron is visible; qexiqi is keshiki in the dictionary's spelling.
Completes the pleasant view sense. Boa viſta provides the favorable scenic interpretation rather than an unrestricted appearance alone.
Fuqen here is not being wise, explained Caxicocarazu. This is a different negative compound from the not-seeing Fuqen below.

runs.text: ſe vſa per ſi ſe não cõ o affirmatiuo juntamen-

lines.note: The dictionary says this form is not used alone but together with its affirmative counterpart. That restriction is a substantive usage observation, not editorial commentary.
Qen, fuqẽtomoni means wise and unwise together. Restored the visible nasal abbreviation over e; without it the Japanese reading would wrongly lose the final n.
Completes the paired wise/unwise gloss. It confirms the conjunction of the two forms described in the usage restriction.
A second Fuqen is not seeing, explained Mizu (見ず). Here mizu is a negative verb, not the water noun, and its single z is retained.

runs.text: Couſa que nem vi, nem ouui, nẽ ſei.

lines.note: Mimon fuqen means neither heard nor seen, with the Portuguese also adding lack of knowledge. The initial fu- continues from the preceding physical row.
Fuqeô and fuqiô name an early-morning time. The scan really prints Polamanhaã here; it is not normalized to the more frequent menhaã form just from a frequency rule.
Completes ante menhaã, before morning. The first vowel differs from manhaã immediately above; the visible variation is retained.
Fuqeracaxi means making a display of something, closely related to fukerakasu. The principal parts ſu, aita remain as printed.

runs.text: ſtra dalgũa couſa que hum tem em estima, ou

lines.note: Specifies the displayed thing as something one esteems. The Portuguese mo-ſtra continuation is kept at its physical boundary.
Completes 'values highly'. This supplies the motivation for display without assuming vanity is the only possible nuance.
Fuqeri denotes taking pride or delight in something. The close-up supports printed etta; it is not simplified to eta on grammatical expectation.
Acuni fuqeru is delighting or immersing oneself in evil. The following Portuguese explicitly says maldade, so the reading is not inferred from a modern homophone.
Completes the evil-indulgence gloss, then starts Miuo fuqeru, self-glorification. The object mi gives the second example a reflexive focus.
Restored Gloriarſe from OCR Cloriarſe. The gloss of pride in oneself agrees with the preceding Miuo phrase; Ta- begins tacara.
Tacara, l, yocuni fuqeru concerns wealth or desire. The text allows these alternatives without requiring that they be identical nouns.

runs.text: tar metido nas riquezas, ou na cobiça. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: Completes being engrossed in riches or covetousness. Itẽ then starts the display-of-valuables sense developed below.
A further Fuqeri, ru means showing a prized object. The principal-part fragment is separately indented, but it continues this semantic discussion.

runs.text: zada como de hum boyão, Catana, &c. Vt,

lines.note: Gives examples of a jar and a Catana. The embedded Japanese weapon word is italic in the scan and remains so; Vt is also italic.
Cudaſaretaru monouo fitobitoni fuqeri means showing others what has graciously been given. The donor honorific belongs to Japanese social phrasing, not a change of object.
Mǒxi ſoro completes the polite statement. Enlargement supports the Portuguese aſoalhoo, with two final o letters; retained that historical spelling rather than the OCR's single o.
Completes showing the gift to everyone and introduces Chauanuo fuqeru. The mark in mostrò is retained without allowing modern tense expectations to decide its shape.
The example is showing a fine tea bowl. Chauan is another italic Japanese word embedded in Portuguese, and its printed gender construction is left unchanged.

runs.text: Hũa erua que tem grandes folhas, &

lines.note: Fuqi names the large-leaved edible plant, fuki. This is a plant entry, distinct from the bellows and verbs that follow.
Completes the statement that it is eaten. The short Portuguese continuation is assigned to the plant rather than the bellows entry.
Fuqi, also fuigo, denotes a smith's or goldsmith's bellows. The connection with blowing is lexical, but the noun must not be silently changed to the following verb.

runs.text: Certa doença contagioſa de febres rijas.

lines.note: Fǔqi is described as a contagious illness with strong fevers. The review does not assign a modern diagnosis merely from this historical label.
Fuqi, qu, uita is illustrated by Caneuo fuqu, smelting metal. The Portuguese Fun continues fundir; the uita principal part is retained as printed.
Completes fundir metal. The action is metallurgical blowing/smelting rather than literally blowing a finished metal object.
The next Fuqi entry concerns scaling fish: Vuo, l, vrocouo fuqu. The visible initial letter and headword support f, not OCR ſ; the Eſcamar catchword anticipates the gloss on the next page.
